newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court to hear line-item veto case in May.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court to hear line-item veto case in May.

text.p: The Supreme Court said Wednesday it would hear arguments quickly in May and then decide a constitutional challenge to a new law that greatly expanded President Clinton's veto power.
Acting on a Clinton administration appeal urging that the historic line-item veto law be upheld as constitutional, the high court scheduled oral arguments for May 27 in the legal showdown.

The May 27 arguments would allow the justices to announce a decision on the law, which gives the president the power to strip items from spending measures without vetoing a whole bill, before the 1996-97 term ends by early July.

The Supreme Court in rare instances has added special argument sessions for landmark cases after the end of its regularly scheduled arguments in mid-April. In recent years, it took that step in cases involving a law that restricted appeals by death-row inmates and in the flag-burning controversy.

The Clinton administration and lawyers for six members of Congress who brought the challenge agreed the Supreme Court should speed up consideration of the line-item veto case. Both sides also agreed the high court should decide the issue.

The law was enacted last year by the Republican-dominated Congress as part of the party's "Contract with America" program and was strongly supported by Clinton, who has yet to use it since it took effect in January.
